newsitem.title: UK: IBCA says may downgrade Booker ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA says may downgrade Booker ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Thursday, it placed the long- and short-term ratings of Booker Plc on RatingWatch negative.
IBCA has a long-term rating of A minus and an A1 short-term rating for Booker.
"This follows yesterday's announcement of the recommended offer by Booker for Nurdin & Peacock, one of the largest wholesale cash and carry businesses in the UK," IBCA said in a statement.

"Although the proposed acquisition is supported by sound business logic and is anticipated to generate cost savings for the combined group, Booker's financial risk is likely to increase at least in the short term," IBCA said.
IBCA said it wanted to appraise the full financial impact of the transaction on the Booker group, partly by discussions with the company.
"The acquisition is intended to be largely debt funded, although around 25 percent of the 264 million stg cost will be funded by equity," IBCA said in a statement.
IBCA said the transaction was contingent upon approval by Booker's shareholders and was also subject to the deal not being referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
